what: EchoStar owns DISH satellite television, the Boost Mobile wireless network, satellite communications through Hughes, and a large holding of wireless spectrum licences. Selling much of that spectrum has reshaped the company.
customers: Satellite and streaming television subscribers, mobile customers on Boost, and enterprise and government satellite communications users.
money: DISH TV and Sling streaming subscriptions
moat: Wireless spectrum licences, which are finite and issued by the government, and which proved to be worth far more than the operating businesses around them.
risks: Satellite television subscribers decline every year
The operating businesses lost money before the spectrum sales
What remains after the spectrum sales is a smaller, structurally challenged business
opportunities: Large gains from spectrum sales transformed the balance sheet, leaving about $14 billion of cash
Analysts see about 47% upside from current levels
Remaining spectrum holdings still have value to mobile operators
watch: What it does with the cash, and subscriber trends at DISH and Boost.
